title: Titanium Compressor Blisk
alloyReason: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V (UNS R56400) is mandated for Titanium Compressor Blisk because its specific strength (290 kN·m/kg) outperforms 4340 steel by 55% and 7075 aluminum by 35% at temperatures up to 400°C. The duplex alpha+beta microstructure provides damage tolerance against high-cycle vibration spectra typical of airframe structures. Its fatigue crack growth rate (da/dN ~2×10^-8 m/cycle at ΔK=20 MPa√m) enables safe-life design for Integral bladed compressor disk (blisk). This rationale is driven by integral bladed compressor disk (blisk) and service environment demands.

faq.q: What corrosion protection is needed for Titanium Compressor Blisk in aerospace environments?
faq.a: Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V naturally forms a protective TiO₂ passive layer that requires no additional coating for corrosion resistance in standard aerospace environments. For integral bladed compressor exposed to hydraulic fluids (Skydrol), de-icing fluids, or marine atmosphere, the passive layer is sufficient. However, galvanic isolation from carbon fiber composites (via fiberglass ply or PTFE sleeve) is required to prevent hydrogen embrittlement.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for Titanium Compressor Blisk orders?
faq.a: Standard lead time for Titanium Compressor Blisk is 15-25 business days depending on quantity and complexity. Rush orders (3-5 working days) are available for prototype evaluation. Sample evaluation (1-5 units) can be expedited to 5-7 business days. Volume pricing is available for production quantities above 100 units.

faq.q: What material certifications are provided with Titanium Compressor Blisk?
faq.a: Each Titanium Compressor Blisk shipment includes EN 10204 Type 3.1 mill test certificate with chemical analysis, mechanical properties, and heat identification. Dimensional inspection reports and Certificate of Conformance (CoC) are standard. First Article Inspection Reports (FAIR) per AS9102 are available on request for integral bladed compressor.
